title: I clicked a suspicious link or typed my password on a fake site: what you can do now
pageTitle: I clicked a suspicious link or typed my password: what you can do now | Spamlock
description: Clicked a link, opened an attachment or typed your password on a fake site? Steps you can take now, depending on what you did: change passwords, call your bank, run a scan.
answer: What to do depends on what you did. Typed a password? Change it, and anywhere else you use it. Gave bank or card details? Call your bank. Opened a file or installed something? Run a scan. If you only opened the page, watch for strange sign-in emails.
stepsTitle: Steps you can take after clicking a suspicious link

steps.title: Close the page
steps.text: Don’t type anything more into it.

steps.title: Typed a password? Change it
steps.text: Change it on that account, and on any other account where you use the same password. Then turn on two-step verification.

steps.title: Gave bank or card details? Call your bank
steps.text: On the number on your card, not one from a message. They can block the card and watch for payments you didn’t make.

steps.title: Opened a file or installed something? Run a scan
steps.text: On a computer, open your antivirus and run a full scan, then let it clean up what it finds. On a phone, delete any app the link asked you to install.

steps.title: Only opened the page?
steps.text: If you didn’t type anything or install anything, you probably don’t need to do more. Watch for sign-in emails and messages you don’t expect.

steps.title: On a work phone or laptop?
Lost money? Report it
steps.text: Tell your bank and report it to the police. In the UK, report it to Report Fraud.

app.title: Check links in the Spamlock app
app.text: Next time, check any link or QR code before you open it.
